AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Neuropathic pain (NP) is a refractory disease in clinic and tremendously impacts on the patients' quality of life. Gene therapy is a potential strategy for the management of NP. In this paper, we examined the analgesic effect and mechanism of hepatocyte growth factor (HGF) in vitro and in vivo.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: We examined the proinflammatroy gene changes in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced BV2 cells with quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) of interleukin (IL)-1β, IL-6, tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, and inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS). Mechanical stimulation tests were performed five times at 5 minute intervals to assess pain thresholds using Von Frey Hair in mice following spared nerve injury (SNI). The glial cell activation of spinal cord was examined by western blot. Statistical significance was determined by Tukey and paired t-test using GraphPad prism 6 software.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: We found that recombinant human HGF protein treatment suppressed LPS-induced BV2 cell activation in vitro, marked by the down-regulation of IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α and iNOS expression, as well as decrease of nitric oxide production. Moreover, intrathecal injection of pUDK-HGF significantly attenuated SNI-induced pain behaviors in mice, through directly inhibition of spinal cord microglia and astrocytes activation.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: Our results indicate that pUDK-HGF can reduce cytotoxicity products released from activated glial cells, which may provide a promising therapeutic strategy for treating NP.
